title: G-code fundamentals: reading a 20-line facing program line by line
summary: Exactly twenty lines of a simulated facing program, with every line explained and the geometry stated.

blocks.eyebrow: Read the tape before you press Cycle Start
blocks.title: Twenty lines that face a part
blocks.body: Read-only simulator exercise, not a machine-ready program. Assume a 3 × 2 in blank centred on X0 Y0, finished face at Z0, rough top at Z+0.020, a 0.500 in flat end mill and verified clearance to fixtures. Units are inches. Speeds and feeds are invented teaching inputs.

items.label: G54: XY stock centre, Z0 finished face; rough stock is above it
Flat end mill in T1 / H1

blocks.heading: Lines 1–5: establish the model
blocks.body: The program number identifies the exercise. Line 2 sets inches, XY plane, absolute mode and G54 while cancelling listed compensation/cycle modes. T1 M06 requests the tool change. G00 G43 H1 Z1.0 explicitly requests rapid positioning with the assumed tool length applied; its path and machine-specific prerequisites must be verified. S3500 M03 commands the example spindle speed and direction.

blocks.heading: Lines 6–8: approach outside the blank
blocks.body: X−2.0 puts the cutter centre 0.500 in beyond the left stock edge. With a 0.250 in cutter radius, its edge has 0.250 in nominal clearance from the stock. Move to Z0.1, then feed to the finished-face height at Z0 while still outside the blank. This geometry says nothing about fixtures; those must also be clear.

blocks.heading: Every line, with its state
rows: Request tool 1 and its tool change
Explicit rapid and length compensation to assumed clearance
Position outside the stock at clearance height
First facing stroke; G01 remains active
Feed step-over outside the right stock edge
Feed step-over outside the left stock edge
Retract under the assumed clearance model
End/reset as defined by the controller
blocks.caption: Simulator-only geometry. No coolant, machine-return routine or production setup approval is implied.

blocks.heading: Lines 18–20: retract, stop, end
blocks.body: Retract to the assumed Z clearance, then stop the spindle and end the program. No G28 or G53 return is included: the appropriate parking path depends on the machine and fixture. A safe return cannot be chosen from the part size alone.

blocks.heading: Words you just watched do work

nodes.title: G00 / G01
nodes.detail: Rapid versus linear feed — never confuse them near stock.

nodes.title: G90 / G91
nodes.detail: Absolute versus incremental. Mixing them without noticing is a classic crash story.

nodes.title: G43 Hn
nodes.detail: Tool length compensation — wrong H offset faces air or the vise.

nodes.title: M06 / M03 / M05 / M30
nodes.detail: Tool change, spindle clockwise, spindle stop and program end; exact behavior follows the controller manual.

items.label: Work coordinates match the stated geometry
items.detail: Here Z0 is the finished face, with rough material above it.

items.label: Tool, fixture and all travel clearances are verified
items.detail: The program does not describe clamps or machine travel limits.

items.label: Controller semantics and startup state are confirmed
items.detail: A generic G-code exercise is not a complete safe-start sequence for every control.

items.label: A qualified operator performs the approved prove-out
items.detail: Use the actual machine procedure and verified cutting data before production.

blocks.title: Dialects differ; the reading skill transfers
blocks.body: Haas, Fanuc, Siemens, and conversational controls spell some parking and coolant codes differently. The point of this page is to read each word as a promise to the machine — not to memorize one builder's macro set.

blocks.heading: Line reading check
blocks.prompt: Line 10 says only Y-0.4. Which motion mode applies?
options: G00 rapid because it is a step-over
No motion because G is omitted
blocks.explanation: G01 remains active until replaced by another motion mode. Line 10 feeds at the active F20.0; an omitted G word does not imply rapid.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct: track the active modal state.
blocks.wrongFeedback: Trace the last explicit motion command before line 10.

blocks.heading: What this tiny program teaches versus what it skips

columns.name: Included
columns.detail: Explicit motion modes, tool length, spindle command, feed approach, five overlapping face passes and retract.

columns.name: Skipped on purpose
columns.detail: Cutter radius comp, canned cycles, subprograms, probing, adaptive clearing — learn those after you can read a face.

blocks.title: Modals remember until cancelled
blocks.body: G01 remains active until another motion command replaces it. Omitting G00 after a cut leaves a feed move; leaving G00 active when a cutting move was intended commands a rapid. Neither the line’s visual position nor its purpose changes the active mode.

blocks.heading: How the X/Y numbers were chosen
items: Stock spans X±1.5 and Y±1.0 in. The cutter radius is 0.250 in.
X endpoints at ±2.0 leave 0.250 in between the cutter edge and nominal stock edge.
Y passes at −0.8, −0.4, 0, 0.4 and 0.8 are 0.400 in apart: a 0.500 in cutter overlaps adjacent sweeps by 0.100 in.
The combined sweep covers Y−1.05 to Y+1.05. This proves nominal coverage only, not fixture clearance or cutting suitability.

slides.title: Rapid above
slides.body: Tool sits at Z1.0, then rapids in X/Y to the start corner while still clear of the part.

slides.title: Feed to Z0
slides.body: Feed to the finished face outside the left edge, with the assumed rough stock at Z+0.020.

slides.title: Cut +X
slides.body: G01 across the face at the facing feed. Chips should look even; a squeal means something else is wrong.

slides.title: Step Y, cut −X
slides.body: Feed Y at the endpoint, then reverse X under the still-active G01. Repeat five strokes and retract.

blocks.heading: Next practice
blocks.body: Change the Y step-over and the X extents on paper, then predict the toolpath before you simulate. Reading beats copying.
